title: Baked Mooncakes with Lotus Seed Paste
summary: Patterned golden mooncakes with a tender, honey-enriched crust wrapped around a smooth sweet lotus seed filling.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: cake flour, plus more for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Alkaline
steps.text: Simmer 240 ml water with ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda for 7-8 min until reduced to about 2 tbsp, then cool and keep only ½ tsp of it.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Beat 147 g honey, the ½ tsp alkaline water, 66 g oil, 240 g cake flour and ½ tsp salt until smooth, then wrap and chill 30 min along with the 340 g lotus seed paste.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough into 6 balls of about 79 g and the paste into 6 balls of about 57 g.

steps.title: Wrap
steps.text: On oiled cling film, roll each dough ball into a 6 mm thick, 12 cm round, set a paste ball in the centre, wrap and press shut, then roll smooth.

steps.title: Press
steps.text: Press each ball into a floured mould onto a lined tray to print the pattern, spacing them 5 cm apart, then freeze 5-10 min.

steps.title: Glaze
steps.text: Heat the oven to 190 °C, whisk 1 egg, 1 egg yolk, 1½ tsp milk and a pinch of salt, and brush two coats over the cakes.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 15-20 min until firm with golden bases, then cool completely on the tray before cutting into quarters.

tips: Only use the small measured amount of alkaline water called for; it's strong, so discard the rest.
Oil your hands and the work surface well, as the dough is quite sticky to handle.
Freeze the shaped cakes briefly before baking to help them hold their imprinted pattern.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keeps 1-2 days in an airtight container, 1 week chilled, or 3 months frozen.
